## What this is

NoteDown is a cross-platform notes app for Android, iOS and the web, in
which every note is a Markdown section and at the same time a to-do.
The project is in its **concept phase**: functional scope and operating
concept (Bedienkonzept) are worked out in `docs/` and in a clickable
**prototype** in `app/` — a real web app, built like the later app would
be, but without a build step, so it can be opened and tested right away.
Once function and look are settled, the target technology is decided and
the prototype is ported (see "Technology direction").

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `docs/requirements.md` | The decided functional scope, by area, each item with its reason |
| `docs/interaction-concept.md` | Cross-cutting operating rules: layout per tier, input, visual language |
| `docs/file-format.md` | The Markdown file NoteDown reads and writes |
| `docs/sync-and-sharing.md` | Sync across devices, sharing single notes, identity without accounts, end-to-end encryption |
| `app/` | The prototype (see "Prototype") |
| `tests/` | Unit tests of the prototype's core logic (`node --test`) |
| `FEATURE_BACKLOG.md` | Ideas not yet decided, with priority and effort |
| `scripts/` | `screenshot.js` (prototype screenshots per tier), `doc-toc.js` (Markdown TOCs), `branch-status.sh` (session-start hook) |

## Device tiers

Every view is designed and checked in these three tiers. The numbers are
the viewports `scripts/screenshot.js --device` uses; the app switches
layout at the CSS widths.

| Tier | Viewport (CSS px) | Input | App layout |
|---|---|---|---|
| desktop | 1440×900 | mouse + hardware keyboard | ≥ 1024 px |
| tablet | 820×1180 portrait | touch only + on-screen keyboard | 600–1023 px |
| phone | 390×844 | touch only + on-screen keyboard | < 600 px |

How a view adapts between the tiers is part of each decision; the rules
that hold for all views are in `docs/interaction-concept.md`.

## Prototype

### Running it

ES modules don't load from `file://`, so the prototype is served by any
static file server from the repo root — no install, no build:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000      # then open http://localhost:8000/app/
```

On a phone in the same network, open `http://<computer-ip>:8000/app/`.
The first start loads the sample notes; ⋮ → "Reset sample notes" brings
them back.

**Dictation needs a secure context** (https or `localhost`): over
`http://<computer-ip>` the browser blocks the microphone. To try it on
a phone, either add the address under Chrome's
`chrome://flags/#unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure`, or open the
prototype with `?dictation=demo`, which replays
`app/sample/dictation.md` instead of listening.

### Structure

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `app/index.html` | The single page |
| `app/css/catppuccin.css` | The four Catppuccin flavors as `--ctp-*` variables (generated from `@catppuccin/palette`, don't edit) |
| `app/css/app.css` | All styles; colors only via the semantic tokens at its top |
| `app/js/core/` | Framework-free logic: file format (`notes-file.js`), Markdown helpers (`markdown.js`), view queries — filter, sort, table of contents (`query.js`), editing commands (`md-commands.js`), multi-select order, copy text and merge (`selection.js`), sync merge of two versions of a file (`merge.js`), sharing helpers — circle names, recovery key, contacts, fake QR grid (`sharing.js`). No DOM access; covered by `tests/*.test.mjs` |
| `app/js/store.js` | App state and persistence (the private file, the shared files and the sync state in `localStorage` for now), moving notes between files, change events |
| `app/js/sync-sim.js` | Prototype only: simulates the server — sync status "syncing" → "synced" after each file change, offline |
| `app/js/ui/` | Views: note list (`note-list.js`, also starts / ends editing), editor (`editor.js` + `live-preview.js`, CodeMirror), toolbar (`toolbar.js`), speech input (`dictation.js`), the + button with hold-to-record (`recorder.js`), multi-select with its action bar and order dialog (`selection.js`), table of contents, menus, snackbar, icons, date labels, the "Sync & sharing" panel (`sync-panel.js`) with its fake QR code and scanner view (`qr.js`) |
| `app/js/main.js` | Wires store and views: top bar, sorting, search, keyboard, prototype options |
| `app/js/sample.js` | Prototype only: loads the sample notes and the sample identity |
| `app/sample/` | `notes.md`: the sample notes, in the real file format — the only source of example content (CLAUDE.md); `sharing.json`: the sample user, devices, contacts and which notes are shared with whom; `dictation.md`: the transcript `?dictation=demo` replays |
| `app/vendor/` | Third-party code, committed as files: `marked` (Markdown rendering), `codemirror.esm.js` (the editor; one bundle of the CodeMirror 6 packages listed in `scripts/vendor/`), each with its license (all MIT) |

Rules: plain HTML/CSS/JS as ES modules, no framework, no external
requests at runtime; third-party code only as a vendored file with its
license. The CodeMirror bundle is the one generated vendor file: to add
an export or update it, edit `scripts/vendor/codemirror.entry.js` /
`package.json` and run `npm install && npm run build` in `scripts/vendor/`
(only needed when changing it — the app itself never needs a build). New logic that doesn't touch the DOM goes into `app/js/core/`
with a unit test.

### Prototype options (variants)

Where a decision is still open, the prototype carries the variants side
by side: ⋮ → "Prototype: …" switches them, and URL parameters preset
them for screenshots and links. Once the user decides, the losing variant
is deleted from code, menu and this table. No variant is open right now.

| Parameter | Values | What it switches |
|---|---|---|
| `flavor` | `system` · `latte` · `frappe` · `macchiato` · `mocha` | Theme (a real setting, not a variant) |
| `view` | `closed` | Start in the archive |
| `dictation` | `demo` | Replay `app/sample/dictation.md` instead of the microphone (not a variant) |
| `reset` | — | Reload the sample notes |
| `sync` | `off` | Start with sync off and no shared files, all sample notes private (reloads the sample notes, like `reset`; not a variant) |

In ⋮ → "Prototype", "Go offline" / "Go online" simulates losing the connection (not a variant); "Reset sample notes" resets notes, shared files and sync state (sync on with the sample identity unless `sync=off`).

### Screenshots

```bash
NODE_PATH="$(npm root -g)" node scripts/screenshot.js --device phone --theme dark \
  --query "view=closed" --out <scratchpad>/shot-phone-dark.png \
  [--eval "<js that opens the state to show>"]
```

The script serves the repo itself, starts each run with empty storage
(so the sample notes load), lists page errors and exits non-zero on
them. Options are documented in its header.

## Technology direction

Not decided yet — that happens once function and look stand. The
prototype is built so that the likely path stays cheap:

- **Favorite: web code in a native shell (Capacitor)** for Android and
  iOS, the same code as a web app / PWA for the browser. The prototype's
  HTML/CSS/ES modules would carry over almost as they are; native
  features (files, speech recognition, app shortcuts) come from Capacitor
  plugins. Obsidian's mobile app is built the same way.
- **Editor:** the Obsidian-style live preview is built on CodeMirror 6
  (round 2), which Obsidian uses for exactly that; it carries over to
  the app as it is.
- **Speech:** the prototype uses the browser's Web Speech API; in the
  app a Capacitor speech-recognition plugin takes its place behind the
  same `startDictation` interface (`app/js/ui/dictation.js`).
- A UI framework, if any, is decided with the port; `app/js/core/` stays
  framework-free either way.
- **Backend** for sync and sharing (`docs/sync-and-sharing.md`): a
  stateless API with a database and an object store that holds only
  encrypted files; language (Python/FastAPI or C#/ASP.NET Core) and
  hosting are decided with the technology. Encryption uses WebCrypto,
  which the browser and the Capacitor web view both offer.
